title: Primitive normalized Borel eigenfunctions in integral rho modules
statement:
Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ and algebraically closed residue field $\kappa=A/\mathfrak m$. Let $H$ be a smooth affine finitely presented group scheme over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, pqf-def-affine-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-affine-spectrum], with the group-object diagrams over this base. Suppose $H$ is split semisimple simply connected: its geometric fibres are connected and have no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup, every central isogeny onto such a fibre from a connected semisimple group is an isomorphism, and choose a split maximal torus $T\subseteq H$ and a Borel subgroup scheme $B\supseteq T$. Here a central isogeny is a surjective group homomorphism with finite central kernel; solvable means that the iterated derived subgroups eventually become trivial; a split torus is a group scheme isomorphic to a product of copies of $\mathbf G_m$; maximal tori and Borel subgroup schemes have, on each geometric fibre, a maximal torus and a maximal smooth connected solvable subgroup, respectively. Write $\mathbf G_m(C)=C^\times$ for every commutative $A$-algebra $C$. A character is a homomorphism of group schemes to $\mathbf G_m$. Let $\Phi^+$ be the positive roots determined by $B$, namely the nonzero characters occurring in the adjoint $T$-action on $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$; the latter is the tangent module at the identity, defined by dual-number points reducing to the identity. In the character lattice $X^*(T)$, addition means multiplication of character values. Use the rational section modules of [lem-sfb-dvr-rho-section-modules], with the following explicit description. Let $\rho\in X^*(T)$ satisfy $2\rho=\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\alpha$, and let $\widetilde\rho:B\to\mathbf G_m$ extend $\rho$ and be trivial on the unipotent radical of $B$. This radical is the subgroup whose geometric fibres are the largest smooth connected normal unipotent subgroups; unipotent means that all geometric points become unipotent matrices in a faithful linear representation. For every integer $m\ge1$, put $$W_m=\{f\in A[H]:f(gb)=\widetilde\rho(b)^m f(g)\text{ for all commutative }A\text{-algebras }C,\ g\in H(C),\ b\in B(C)\}.$$ Evaluation of $f$ means pullback of the regular function along its $C$-point. Use the left-translation action $(h f)(g)=f(h^{-1}g)$. A rational $H$-module is an $A$-module $M$ with an $A$-linear coaction $M\to M\otimes_A A[H]$ satisfying the counit and coassociativity identities, where $A[H]=\Gamma(H,\mathcal O_H)$ is the coordinate Hopf algebra. Its invariants are $M^H=\{x:\rho_M(x)=x\otimes1\}$. Equivariant maps commute with coactions; tensor products have diagonal coaction. These identities are tested after every commutative $A$-algebra extension, not just on $A$-points. Let $V\subseteq B$ be its unipotent radical. Suppose $n_0\in N_H(T)(A)$ induces the Weyl element reversing $\Phi^+$, and multiplication $V\times_A B\to H$, $(u,b)\mapsto u n_0b$, is an open immersion whose image is dense in every geometric fibre of $H$. Here normalizing means preserving $T$ by conjugation, and the action on characters is $(w\chi)(t)=\chi(n_0^{-1}tn_0)$. Then for every integer $m\ge1$ there is $f_m\in W_m$ such that $f_m(n_0)=1$ and
$$f_m(bg)=\widetilde\rho(b)^{-m}f_m(g)$$
for every commutative $A$-algebra $C$, $b\in B(C)$ and $g\in H(C)$. This is an identity of regular functions on $B\times_A H$, not just an identity on $A$-points.

source.place: Agent integral-lattice argument extending Proposition 22.22 and the longest-cell calculation in Theorem 21.80, printed pp.450--451,468--470. The proposed argument is retained in report.md; Alper §9.7 motivates the application, not a claim that Milne states the DVR result.

proof.text: Fix $m\ge1$. Write $\psi=\widetilde\rho^m$, $R=A[H]$, $D=A[B]$, $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ and $E=\overline K$. By [lem-sfb-dvr-rho-section-modules], the actual submodule $W=W_m\subset R$ is nonzero finite free and its left-translation action is a rational coaction. The DVR is a Noetherian local ring by [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal]. A smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup of a geometric fibre is solvable by [lem-sfb-smooth-unipotent-solvable]; hence the semisimple fibres are reductive. Apply [lem-sfb-local-borel-quotient-geometry]: $B=T\ltimes V$, $B$ and $V$ are smooth, and these groups and the positive-root sets have the stated geometric base-change compatibility. Smoothness and [sbc-lem-smooth-criterion], followed by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion], make both $R$ and $D$ flat over $A$. Thus they are torsion-free by [lem-trf-flat-module-torsionfree-domain].

proof.text: Right multiplication $r:H\times_A B\to H$ defines $d:R\to R\otimes_A D$ by $d(f)=r^*f-f\otimes\psi$. Testing the universal point of this affine product shows $W=\ker d$. The field $K$ is a flat $A$-module by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat], and $E$ is a flat $K$-module by [lem-weil-pbc-module-over-field-flat]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] successively with $K$ and $E$ to $0\to W\to R\xrightarrow d R\otimes_A D$. Consequently $W_K$ and $W_E$ are precisely the right-$\psi$ semi-invariant regular-function modules on $H_K$ and $H_E$, respectively. Here affine base change replaces coordinate algebras and the multiplication pullback by their tensor products, by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] and its displayed projection maps. The left-translation coaction base changes to the same left-translation coaction on these kernels. In particular $W_E\ne0$, since a nonempty finite basis of $W$ remains a nonempty basis after scalar extension.

proof.text: Identify $X^*(T_E)$ with $\mathbf Z^r$ by the chosen splitting. Since $n_0$ reverses the positive roots, $2w_0\rho_E=-\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi_E^+}\alpha=-2\rho_E$; the character lattice has no $2$-torsion, so $w_0\rho_E=-\rho_E$, also when $E$ has characteristic $2$. Thus $W_E=E_{B_E}(-m\widetilde\rho_E)$ in the convention of [lem-sfb-induced-module-primitive-line]. All its hypotheses hold: $E$ is algebraically closed, $H_E$ is semisimple simply connected, and Step 1 supplies the split Borel decomposition and the compatible positive roots. This node gives a nonzero $V_E$-fixed line with $T_E$-weight $w_0(-m\rho_E)=m\rho_E$. For $b=tu$, its vectors therefore satisfy $b v=\psi(b)v$, since $u$ fixes them and $\psi$ is trivial on $V_E$. The cited identities are coaction identities, so this conclusion holds over every $E$-algebra, not only on $E$-points.

proof.text: Restrict the rational coaction on $W$ along $B\hookrightarrow H$ and define the $A$-linear map $e:W\to W\otimes_A D$ by $e(w)=c_B(w)-w\otimes\psi$. Thus $e(w)=0$ means precisely $b w=\psi(b)w$ for left translation. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact], with the same flat scalar extensions of Step 2, to $0\to\ker e\to W\xrightarrow e W\otimes_A D$. It identifies $(\ker e_K)\otimes_K E$ with $\ker e_E$. Step 3 gives a nonzero member of $\ker e_E$, whence $\ker e_K\ne0$: the tensor product of the zero space is zero. Choose $0\ne v_K\in\ker e_K$. This descends the eigenvector equations; it does not assert that invariants commute with reduction to the residue field.

source.place: Tag 00HD, lemma-flat, preservation of injections and exact sequences; Tag 00HT, lemma-flat-localization, (1). Agent-written application to the explicit semi-invariance and eigenvector kernels.

proof.text: Choose a finite basis $a_1,\ldots,a_s$ of $W$ and write $v_K=\sum_i c_i a_i$ with $c_i\in K$. Let $\pi$ be a uniformizer and let $q$ be the minimum of the integer valuations of the nonzero $c_i$. Then $w=\pi^{-q}v_K$ has all coordinates in $A$ and at least one a unit; hence $w\in W\setminus\pi W$. This uses the discrete valuation description of a DVR in [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Since $W$ is finite free and $D$ is torsion-free, $W\otimes_A D$ is a finite direct sum of copies of $D$ and injects into its localization over $K$. The equality $e_K(w)=0$ therefore implies $e(w)=0$. For every $A$-algebra $C$ this says $w(b^{-1}g)=\psi(b)w(g)$; replacing $b$ by $b^{-1}$ gives $w(bg)=\psi(b)^{-1}w(g)$. These equations hold at universal affine points and hence as identities of regular functions.

source.place: Definition 22.21 and Proposition 22.22, printed pp.468--469. The extension from the geometric generic fibre to the DVR and the primitive reduction argument are agent-written.

proof.text: The image $\bar w$ of $w$ in $R/\pi R=\kappa[H_\kappa]$ is nonzero. Indeed multiplication by $\pi$ on $R$ is injective, and tensoring this injection with the flat $A$-module $D$ stays injective by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact]. Thus $R\otimes_A D$ has no $\pi$-torsion. If $w=\pi h$ for $h\in R$, then $0=d(w)=\pi d(h)$, so $d(h)=0$ and $h\in W$. This contradicts $w\notin\pi W$. This is the required saturation argument; the inclusion $W\subset R$ alone would not justify nonzero reduction. Both equivariance identities for $w$ now reduce to regular-function identities for $\bar w$ on the closed fibre.

source.place: Tag 00HD, lemma-flat, preservation of injections and exact sequences; Tag 00HT, lemma-flat-localization, (1). Agent-written application to the explicit semi-invariance and eigenvector kernels.

proof.text:
By [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced], $H_\kappa$ is reduced. The assumed cell map $j_\kappa:V_\kappa\times_\kappa B_\kappa\to H_\kappa$ is a dense open immersion. Its source and target are affine, so it is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Apply [lemma-nagata-reduced-dense-image-schematic] and [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image]: its schematic image is all of $H_\kappa$ and the kernel of the structure-sheaf map is zero. Hence restriction $\kappa[H_\kappa]\to\kappa[V_\kappa\times B_\kappa]$ is injective. Left $V$-invariance from Step 5 and right equivariance from $w\in W$ give, at universal points,
$$\bar w(u\bar n_0 b)=\bar w(\bar n_0 b)=\bar\psi(b)\bar w(\bar n_0).$$
If $\bar w(\bar n_0)=0$, the restriction to the cell is zero and injectivity forces $\bar w=0$, contradicting Step 6. Thus the scalar $w(n_0)\in A$ has nonzero residue in $\kappa$ and is a unit in the local ring $A$.

source.place: Definition 22.21 and Proposition 22.22, printed pp.468--469. The extension from the geometric generic fibre to the DVR and the primitive reduction argument are agent-written.

proof.text: Set $f_m=w(n_0)^{-1}w$. Since $W$ is an $A$-submodule, $f_m\in W_m$, and evaluation gives $f_m(n_0)=1$. Multiplying the regular-function identity of Step 5 by the scalar $w(n_0)^{-1}$ gives $f_m(bg)=\widetilde\rho(b)^{-m}f_m(g)$ on $B\times_A H$. Pullback gives the same formula over every commutative $A$-algebra. The argument works for each $m\ge1$.
